title: Volume of an Open Box Built from a Square Sheet
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: From a $12\times 12$ square sheet, identical squares of side $x$ are cut from the four corners and the flaps are folded up to form an open box. Model the box volume $V(x)$ and determine the admissible range of $x$.

steps.title: Identify the Box Height
steps.explanation: Folding the cut edges upright makes the removed square's side $x$ the height of the box.
steps.why: The fold line sits exactly $x$ in from each edge.

steps.title: Derive the Base Side Length
steps.explanation: Each $12$-unit edge loses an $x$-length segment at both ends, leaving a square base of side $12-2x$.
steps.why: Both corners of every edge are cut, hence the factor of two.

steps.title: Assemble the Volume Function
steps.explanation: Base area $(12-2x)^2$ times height $x$ gives the cubic volume model.
steps.why: Volume of a rectangular box is base area multiplied by height.

steps.title: Bound the Cut Size
steps.explanation: A cut must be positive, and two cuts cannot consume more than the full $12$-unit edge; at $x=6$ the sheet disappears entirely.
steps.why: Geometric feasibility, not the algebra, restricts the model's domain.
